params.body:
The Sources page showed 35 sources under "Needs a look" on 9 November 2026, nearly all web-browse pages, and two adapters failing. Checked one by one: twelve of those pages refuse a fetch of the page while their feed answers, six addresses are dead or a duplicate, and fifteen sites refuse a fetch and publish no feed. Wikipedia failed 74 runs in a row because Wikimedia had published nothing after 6 November.

## What changes

**A page that keeps failing is read from its feed** (`packages/core/feed-instead.mjs`, called from `collect.mjs` before parking). The pipeline looked for a feed only when a person saved a source (`resolveSourceUrl`); a source that came in as a page stayed a page. Now a web-browse source that has failed three times in a row (`SOURCE_FEED_AFTER`, default 3) gets its feed looked for once, with the discovery that already exists. A feed that parses becomes what is read: same id, state, sectors and history, type `rss`, failures from nought, the old page in a new column `page_url`, the reason in its notes. No feed, or a feed another source already reads: nothing changes and parking goes on as before. `feed_checked_at` makes it once; clear it to look again.

**`bin/repair-sources.mjs`**, run by a person, dry unless `--apply`:
- With `research/source-repairs-2026-11-09.json`: the sources from that list, found by the address the Sources page shows. 12 go to a feed (three of them because the address itself was wrong: Reuters Institute, Another Magazine, and "Esports Insider", which pointed at esports.gg), 21 are muted with the reason in their notes. Every feed was checked with the collector's own User-Agent on 9 November. An address that matches no page or more than one is named and left alone.
- With `--parked`: the feed of every page the collector parked (35 on the page) is looked for once; a page whose feed answers is read from it and switched back on (unmute, so admitted again, by the person who runs it).

**`wikipedia-spikes`** reads the latest day Wikimedia has published, up to three days back, instead of yesterday only. A 404 is "not published yet", not a failure; when no language has anything for three days, the run is skipped with that reason. Another refusal still fails. One more fix on the same line: a page the adapter had read before was skipped without counting towards the ten a language, and the adapter has no cadence, so each collect round could take ten more of the same day. Read-before now counts. This follows from the code; I could not compare it with the intake numbers, since the workbench is not admitted to read on this project.

## On the box, after merge and deploy

```bash
node bin/repair-sources.mjs research/source-repairs-2026-11-09.json --by=<name>           # dry
node bin/repair-sources.mjs research/source-repairs-2026-11-09.json --by=<name> --apply
node bin/repair-sources.mjs --parked --by=<name>                                          # dry, fetches each parked page
node bin/repair-sources.mjs --parked --by=<name> --apply
```

The dry run of `--parked` fetches every parked page and its candidate feeds, so it takes a few minutes.

## Not in this PR

The 158 cited publishers in New Sources G. are a review queue, not failures.

## Tests

`npm test`: 1603 of 1603. `tsc`: clean. New: `test/feed-instead.test.mjs` (switch, once only, no second row for one feed, the plan dry and applied, parked pages), `test/wikipedia-spikes.test.mjs` (latest day, a stretch skipped, read-before counts, another refusal fails).
params.title: Read failing pages from their feed; Wikipedia reads the latest published day
